questions.subject: Physics
questions.q: Two containers C1 and C2 of volumes V and 4V respectively, hold the same ideal gas and are connected by a thin horizontal tube of negligible volume with a valve which is initially closed. The initial pressures of the gas in C1 and C2 are p and 5p, respectively. Heat baths are employed to maintain the temperatures in the containers at 300 K and 400 K, respectively. The valve is now opened. Select the correct statement.
options: The gas will flow from the hot container to the cold one and the process is reversible.
The gas will flow from one container to the other till the number of moles in two containers are equal.
A long time after the valve is opened, the pressure in both the containers will be <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><mn>3</mn><mi>p</mi></math>.
A long time after the valve is opened, number of moles of gas in the hot container will be thrice that of the cold one.
questions.solution:
Let n1 and n2 are number of moles of gas present in container C1 and C2 respectively, before the value is opened.

Then, using pV=nRT.

n1=pVR300

and n2=5p4VR400

When value is opened gas flows from C2 to C1 till pressure in C1 and C2 is equal. Let after equalisation of pressure in both C1 and C2, its value is p0,

Then, using pV=nRT.

p0V=n1'R300 (Container C1)

and p04V=n2'R400 (Container C2)

So, n1'=p0VR300

As no gas is leaked from containers, 

n1+n2=n1':n2'

⇒pVR300+20pVR400

=p0VR300+4p0VR400

So, p1300+20400=p01300+4400

⇒4p=p0

Now, n2'n1'=4p0VR400p0VR300=3

Finally number of moles of C2 is thrice of C1.

Change in internal energy of n moles of an ideal gas, when temperature changes by ΔT is

=f2nRΔT=f2Δp·V

where, f= degree of freedom. Hence, we have

Now, using γ=1+2f

where, γ= ratio of specific heats = adiabatic index.

So, equation of adiabats can be written as pVγ= constant ⇒pV7/5= constant

⇒p5V7= constant

options: <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> increases and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> decreases and the total entropy remains the same

<math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>1</mn></msub></math> decreases and <math xmlns="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML"><msub><mi>U</mi><mn>2</mn></msub></math> increases and the total entropy remains the same

questions.solution:
By second law of thermodynamics, entropy of a system either increases or remains constant (only in reversible quasistatic processes).

Also, from graphs given
S2>S1⇒QT2>QT1

where, S is entropy, Q is heat and T is the temperature.
or T1<T2

Hence, temperature of system 1 is less than system 2. So, heat flows from system 2 to system 1.

Hence, U1 increases and U2 decreases.

questions.q: A container with rigid walls is covered with perfectly insulating material. The container is divided into two parts by a partition. One part contains a gas while the other is fully evacuated (vacuum). The partition is suddenly removed. The gas rushes to fill the entire volume and comes to equilibrium after a little time. the initial entropy of the gas equals its final entropy
questions.solution: expansion is against vacuum $\therefore \Delta \mathrm{W}=0$ Insulated container $\therefore \Delta \mathrm{Q}=0$ First law of thermodynamics $\begin{array}{l} \Delta \mathrm{Q}=\Delta \mathrm{W}+\Delta \mathrm{U} \\ 0=0+\Delta \mathrm{U} \\ 0=0+\Delta \mathrm{U} \\ \Delta \mathrm{U}=0 \end{array}$
